answer_in_one_paragraph: As a graph of where a course can go, the atlas is 108 pieces: 86 dynamics alone, the largest 30. Counting only links that carry a law it is 114 pieces, the largest 12; the piece of 30 hangs on 12 exits that no law shows. The capture family, home of the meta-attractor, has one of 17 dynamics linked by a law, though its Lean modules import one another in a chain. No atlas link runs from a lock to turning or from turning to renewal; TurningInTime proves the first. Cancer (confined-rise-within-a-whole) is alone, on the carrier the line on a stock uses. The centre's seven exits end in words that existing dynamics already name.
